title: Top 5 Deadliest Animals to Humans
hook: These animals take out more humans than anything else, and number one? It's tiny. Like, really tiny.

items.name: Assassin Bugs
items.line: Assassin bugs spread Chagas disease, which kills more than ten thousand people every year.

items.name: Freshwater Snails
items.line: Yeah, snails. Tiny freshwater snails spread a parasite that kills about fourteen thousand people a year.

items.name: Dogs
items.line: Rabies kills about forty four thousand people a year, and dogs cause up to ninety nine percent of those cases.

items.name: Snakes
items.line: Snakebites kill between eighty one thousand and one hundred thirty eight thousand people every single year.

items.name: Mosquitoes
items.line: Mosquitoes spread malaria, which killed about six hundred ten thousand people in twenty twenty four alone.

outro: Okay be honest, which one scares you the most? Drop it below.
description: The animals behind the most human deaths each year (not counting humans), based on World Health Organization estimates.
sources: WHO malaria fact sheet (610,000 deaths in 2024)
WHO snakebite envenoming fact sheet (81,410–137,880 deaths/year)
WHO rabies fact sheet (44,203 deaths/year, up to 99% dog-transmitted)
WHO Chagas disease fact sheet (more than 10,000 deaths/year)

title: The 5 Fastest Animals on the Planet
hook: Number one moves faster than a Formula One car. And yeah, it's an animal.

items.name: Cheetah
items.line: The cheetah, fastest on land, has been reliably clocked at about one hundred four kilometers per hour.

items.name: Free-Tailed Bat
items.line: A free tailed bat was tracked at around one hundred sixty kilometers per hour in level flight. A bat!

items.name: Needletail Swift
items.line: The white throated needletail is the fastest bird in flapping flight, at about one hundred sixty nine kilometers per hour.

items.name: Golden Eagle
items.line: A diving golden eagle can hit two hundred forty kilometers per hour, maybe even more.

items.name: Peregrine Falcon
items.line: The peregrine falcon dives at up to three hundred eighty nine kilometers per hour. Faster than a Formula One car.

outro: Did you think a bird would take number one? Be honest.
description: The fastest animals on Earth ranked by top recorded speed (dives included). Speeds are approximate and some measurements are debated.
sources: McCracken et al. 2016, Royal Society Open Science (free-tailed bat flight speed)

title: The 5 Deepest Places in the Ocean
hook: Number one is deeper than Mount Everest is tall. Let that sink in.

items.name: Izu-Ogasawara Trench
items.line: Off Japan, the Izu Ogasawara Trench drops about nine thousand eight hundred meters.

items.name: Kermadec Trench
items.line: New Zealand's Kermadec Trench goes past ten thousand meters down.

items.name: Philippine Trench
items.line: The Philippine Trench sinks about ten thousand five hundred forty meters, right off Mindanao.

items.name: Tonga Trench
items.line: The Tonga Trench's Horizon Deep reaches about ten thousand eight hundred meters.

items.name: Mariana Trench
items.line: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is almost eleven kilometers down, with crushing pressure over a thousand times the surface.

outro: Would you go down there in a submarine? Because I'm good.
description: The deepest ocean trenches on Earth, ranked by their deepest measured point. Depths are approximate and vary slightly between surveys.
sources: Five Deeps Expedition / Caladan Oceanic 2019–2022 dive measurements
Linley et al. 2017, Deep Sea Research Part I (Kermadec 10,047 m)

title: The 5 Biggest Planets in Our Solar System
hook: You could fit over a thousand Earths inside number one. Wild, right?

items.name: Earth
items.line: Earth is about twelve thousand seven hundred kilometers wide, the biggest rocky planet.

items.name: Neptune
items.line: Neptune is nearly four times wider than Earth and has the fastest winds in the solar system.

items.name: Uranus
items.line: Uranus is just a bit wider than Neptune and spins tipped over on its side.

items.name: Saturn
items.line: Saturn is over nine times wider than Earth and light enough that it would float in water.

items.name: Jupiter
items.line: Jupiter is so huge that more than thirteen hundred Earths could fit inside it.

outro: Which planet are you visiting first? Tell me below.
description: The largest planets in our solar system ranked by diameter, using NASA figures.

title: The 5 Highest Mountains on Earth
hook: All five are in Asia, and number one is still growing. Every single year.

items.name: Makalu
items.line: Makalu, on the Nepal China border, rises eight thousand four hundred eighty five meters.

items.name: Lhotse
items.line: Lhotse stands eight thousand five hundred sixteen meters, right next door to Everest.

items.name: Kangchenjunga
items.line: Kangchenjunga reaches eight thousand five hundred eighty six meters and was once thought to be the tallest.

items.name: K2
items.line: K2 is eight thousand six hundred eleven meters, and far deadlier to climb than Everest.

items.name: Mount Everest
items.line: Mount Everest stands eight thousand eight hundred forty nine meters and still rises a few millimeters every year.

outro: Would you ever try climbing number one? Comment yes or no.
description: The highest mountains in the world ranked by elevation above sea level.
sources: Nepal and China joint survey (2020) for Everest

title: The 5 Largest Deserts in the World
hook: The biggest desert on Earth? It's not even hot. Watch this.

items.name: Gobi Desert
items.line: The Gobi in Mongolia and China covers about one point three million square kilometers.

items.name: Arabian Desert
items.line: The Arabian Desert spans about two point three million square kilometers.

items.name: Sahara Desert
items.line: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert, about the size of the entire United States.

items.name: Arctic Desert
items.line: The Arctic counts as a desert because it gets so little rain or snow, covering about fourteen million square kilometers.

items.name: Antarctic Desert
items.line: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth, at about fourteen million square kilometers of ice.

outro: Did you know Antarctica counts as a desert? Yes or no, be honest.
description: The world's largest deserts by area. A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat.
